evals.prompt: I run a bakery in one town in England, about 300 Instagram followers. I have $150 total. What should I give away to get more local customers in the door?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the bakery's own product or in-store credit, redeemed in person, with several small winners or a repeat-visit structure. Explains why a broad prize would pull non-locals. Gives an estimate-labelled budget within $150 including any signage or promotion, two alternatives (one larger prize, a local partner bundle), a short adaptable description, and one next decision. Makes no entrant-count promise and does not cite the dataset as proof of results. For the stated location, keeps one local-rules line naming the country and a concrete question for the reader's own lawyer, without stating a legal requirement.
assertions: Preferred prize is own product or store credit redeemed locally
States why a broad-appeal prize suits this objective poorly
Budget lines are labelled estimates and total at or under $150
Offers two alternatives of different category or structure
Ends on a concrete next decision
Does not promise entrant numbers
For the stated location, keeps one local-rules line naming the country and a concrete question for the reader's own lawyer, without stating a legal requirement.

evals.prompt: We sell accounting software for freelancers. Marketing wants to give away a PS5 to get sign-ups. Good idea?

Says when it can still work (pure reach with a qualification step afterward) and when it fails (leads going straight to trials or sales). Offers on-brand alternatives such as a free annual plan, an accountant session, or a work-setup bundle, or a way to keep the PS5 tied to the product. States that the dataset cannot show which option performs better.
assertions: Names the audience mismatch and the missing connection to the business
Distinguishes the reach objective from the lead-quality objective
Offers at least two on-brand alternatives
States that the dataset cannot rank the options
Gives a keep, adjust or replace verdict
Where the aim is leads, prefers a Prize that only a buyer values and says the dataset holds no outcome after the entry

Recommends one structure and ties it to the subscriber-who-buys objective
